name: Tucked In
description: Three-piece indie folk-rock group (Gunnar Teel, Shae Ferguson, Dan Rodgers) that started as a Brooklyn duo and relocated to the Phoenixville area. Their songs draw on life in suburban Pennsylvania.
activity: 2025 'Roughest Roads' Northeast tour behind third EP Saints and Cannons, including a Sept 12, 2025 hometown show at the Colonial Theatre, Phoenixville (also Sherman Showcase, Stroudsburg, June 27, 2025).

name: Clockwork Stenographer
description: Guitar-bass-drums trio playing what they call sad rock from the Philadelphia suburbs. Their debut EP was tracked at Gradwell House in NJ.
activity: Debut EP 'Orbits' released on Bandcamp Sept 20, 2025; Bandcamp location Ambler, PA. No show dates found.

name: XIII PFP
description: Veteran Lansdale/BuxMont hardcore band that came back after roughly a decade away. Their return show was a benefit for the Pennsylvania Immigration Resource Center.
activity: Reunion show Nov 8, 2025 at Poppy's Tavern, Hatfield; co-headlined an all-ages show with Dysphoria at Poppy's Tavern on Feb 20, 2026 (North Penn Now / Central Bucks News, Feb 13, 2026).

name: Dysphoria
description: Lansdale hardcore quintet formed in 1993, a long-running name in the Pennsylvania hardcore scene. They have played This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia over the years.
activity: Played The Polish Club, Phoenixville on Dec 20, 2025 (setlist.fm) and co-headlined Poppy's Tavern, Hatfield on Feb 20, 2026 with XIII PFP.

name: L.M.I.
description: Lansdale band mixing stoner rock heft with punk and hardcore. They have a string of numbered releases plus a split with Vulturepeak.
activity: Opened XIII PFP's Nov 8, 2025 benefit show at Poppy's Tavern, Hatfield (North Penn Now / Central Bucks News, Nov 6, 2025). Latest Bandcamp release: L.M.I. V.

name: The Wonder Years
description: Pop-punk band formed in Lansdale that grew into one of the genre's best-known acts. They are now usually billed as a Philadelphia band.
activity: Released 'No Closer to Heaven' 10th anniversary edition Oct 14, 2025, and toured on it in 2026 (including Theatre of Living Arts, Philadelphia, April 2026).

name: The Last Big Band
description: 17-piece jazz orchestra founded in 2002 by trombonist Jim Zoller and trumpeter Roger Morgan. It plays swing-era and newer big-band charts, including originals by its own arrangers, at a monthly residency in downtown Pottstown.
activity: Monthly shows at Rivet Canteen & Assembly, Pottstown through 2026 (May 13 and June 10, 2026 listed; Nov 11, 2026 listed on Eventbrite); played Towamencin's summer series at Fischer's Park, Lansdale, on July 30, 2026.
